reviews.comment: Dr. Miller is an exceptional professor. His lectures were engaging, the material was interesting, and the class fostered lively discussion. I highly recommend
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Caring

reviews.comment: Glen Miller is awesome. Truly fell in love with his class and studying philosophy as an electrical engineering major! Conversations were super awesome in his class and his tests weren't too hard as long as you took notes and made your notecard he gives you. Be prepared to not get grades back early at all but overall he became a dear friend to me!

Dr. Miller is excellent if you actually want to learn something in your PHIL course. He loves to engage with his students and is very encouraging. He can be a slow grader. If you are willing to engage during class you shouldn't have to worry. If you want to skip don't take him you do need to be in class to learn the exam content.
reviews.ratingTags: Caring--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller knows a lot because he thinks a lot about ethics! If you engage with him during class you will learn a lot.
reviews.ratingTags: Inspirational--Respected

reviews.comment: While reading is required, the reading is very interesting, and you have to fully understand what you are reading in order to be able to participate in class actively, which is also required for a grade. He really makes you work for the grade, and the exams are difficult, but despite both of those things the class discussions are very interesting.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr.Miller cares about his classes and students, but is absolutely not an easy A. Do not expect scores back on pretty much any work you do for his class, until the day they are due at the end of the semester. I recommend his office hours because he does provide helpful feedback there. I would not take this prof again.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Caring

reviews.comment: I genuinely believe that this is the worst professor employed at Texas A&M University. He was three months behind on grading. He gives bad grades with zero explanation or critiques. Literally do not take this class, or any class that he teaches, no matter what.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am one of Dr. Miller's TAs. Do not take this class unless it is necessary. Period.

Like all philosophy professors, heavy on the reading. However it was still very accessible for me as an engineering student. He is a very fair professor, and will make you earn your grade, so definitely not a blow off class. I would strongly recommend him though.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I think I learned more in this class than I have in any other at A&M, which goes to show how good of a professor Dr. Miller is. You should take this class if you want to work on critical thinking skills, enjoy learning, and want to learn about AI ethics.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Caring--Respected

reviews.comment: Do not take him. He requires impossible amounts of reading each week (10-14 pages) and will include incredibly specific questions from these readings on the test. The class is very theory heavy and rarely includes practical applications. There is a 2.5 deduction from your final grade per class that you miss. His ego is also huge and unbearable.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Requirement for certain engineering majors. Class is theory heavy, with little practical application. Exams are difficult multiple choice on minor differences between theories. Tons of reading, which you need to do well. Grade is dependant on your TA - Mine graded everything like she was battalion commander of the SS. Too hard for no reason.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I did not enjoy this class, but I respect Mr. Miller. He cares about his subject deeply. Engineers are forced to take this class and I believe most of the information and philosophies taught will never be used by us again. He makes the class harder than it needs to be.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller provided great information in class, but you did have to pay attention to the specifics to do well on the exams. His in class discussions were fun and helpful in understanding the topics we were going over, and he would provide insight into getting thoughts going. Overall I would take this class again and I really enjoyed Dr. Miller.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Miller! I will say, his teaching style is not for everyone. Most lectures are Socratic and discuss the reading as new ideas pop up in class throughout the discussion. Dr. Miller is very smart and wants his students to succeed. There are occasional pop quizzes and the lectures are necessary to do well on the tests, so show up!
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller is an excellent lecturer and this class was super interesting. As long as you come prepared to class (doing the readings), you should be pretty well prepared for the in-class discussions. His tests are really fair and by doing the work you should get an A in the class.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller is a fair but difficult professor. You often feel like you are struggling more than you really are while working with him. The class is a lot of work (2 free response exams, a paper, a presentation, and a final assignment), but the work you put in is what you get out of the class. He's also very interactive, so introverts beware.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller makes lectures entertaining by analyzing many different case studies, and then allowing groups to discuss how they would have handled various situations. If you show up, read, do your work, and understand weekly learning objectives, you will get an A.Shook hands with him after the final. Great guy. Recitations were boring at times(TA)...
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Took Ethics of Artificial Intelligence. Great professor who loves the subject. A bit heavy on the philosophy side of things. Definitely doable for a computer science (or non phil) major. Interesting class I would definitely recommend taking.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
clearly very experienced, knowledgeable, and approachable, with clear deadlines and expectations for the class.
only complaint was that classes were discussion based so sometimes discussions could be derailed or dominated by certain people; would've preferred more ways for everybody to contribute in a more organized fashion.

Dr. Miller exposed us to a wide variety of ideas in the field of digital ethics, but he also leaves a lot of the discussion up to the direction the class goes, so your experience in class will also depend a lot on the other students. I really enjoyed this class. Be ready for a good amount of reading and come to class prepared to discuss.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller gave inspirational lectures and made this class super enjoyable. The content can be tough, but if you do the assignments when youre supposed to, you will be on track to understand everything and do well in the class. The recitations are super helpful too! And you actually get to know your classmates because theyre pretty small sections
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lots of reading. Exams based of what you've read. 2 books mandatory to buy. 2 exams (including final), pop-quizzes. Exam lets you use one sheet of paper with whatever HANDWRITTEN notes on it. ALL exam questions are open-ended. Lecture notes created from class participation/discussions. Assignments/projects turned in online.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller is a good lecturer, who really knows what he is talking about. Even if you are not interested in the topic of ethics, he finds ways to make it interesting for all.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller gives great lectures, and often lets the class direct itself. As someone who loves participating in class, it's great to have the lecture be dictated by how the students interpreted the reading. There is extremely heavy reading, but I've managed to squeak by so far even when I forget to do the reading.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Millers class isn't very hard but requires a lot of reading. That being said your tests are based off of random things said during class. You can spend an entire class on a discussion that has nothing to do with the class. He is a nice professor but doesn't reply to emails and is very disorganized.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Miller was one of the first professors at TAMU who made me feel like they really cared about their student's education. Interesting lectures and overall great discussions in every class.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller is just an okay professor. The class though as a whole is extremely annoying. I feel like they try to just shove as much work onto the students as possible. It feels like they know that engineers have classes that are much more difficult and they're trying to compete. My TA was not very nice either, ironically insensitive.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor is a great guy, no doubt about it, he really makes you learn in his class. However, do not take this class if what you are looking for is a blow off class. Be expected to have a quiz every class. Also, there are several readings assigned every class. This class is also participation HEAVY, if you are shy, I wouldn't recommend this class.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller is a very good professor who loves his students. You will never be bored in class as he forces you to participate. There is a lot of reading associated with this class as well as pop quizzes over the reading at the beginning of class. The quizzes are very easy and the tests are difficult but very much doable as it is open notes.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: It's a pretty easy class. Just be sure to do the writing assignments and show up. It was actually a pretty fun class, with much more discussion than computer science/math classes.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: You're supposed to read a bunch, but I didn't and still clutched an A. Don't skip too much or else they bone you with -2.5 pts off entire grade for every UE absence past 2. Do the online sessions, cram quizlets, don't write s**t papers and you'll be fine. He's a pretty chill guy and lectures can be fun. Grade is almost entirely on your TA, though.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Easy to get a B, requires work to get an A. Read the textbook and all the assigned readings before class like they tell you to. If you do that, and put forth reasonable effort into studying and essays, you'll probably make an A. If you don't do that, you'll make a B. Miller is a great professor, can't go wrong with Miller.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Great class, great professor. Work load is intense, but rewarding. Read the textbook and philosophy papers if you want an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures
